text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.16% today after oil prices dropped sharply on renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Iran conflict. On October 27th, news that Iran's supreme leader and top security officials were discussing conditions to end the war pushed oil prices lower—US crude fell to $107.89, down from the spike above $116 just days earlier. Since the stock had climbed 5.11% over the past two weeks on the back of rising geopolitical tensions and higher oil prices, today's pullback reflects investors unwinding those gains as the immediate risk of wider conflict receded.

The volatility tracks the regional tension cycle: fears of Saudi infrastructure damage and supply disruptions pushed oil and the stock higher earlier in the week, but signs of diplomatic progress—Saudi Arabia's de-escalation talks with Iran on October 26th, followed by the supreme leader's comments on October 27th—reversed that momentum. Energy stocks like ConocoPhillips are sensitive to these swings because their profits move directly with oil prices.
